A '''crab tracer''' was a type of [[Homing beacon/Legends|tracking device]]. In [[19 ABY/Legends|19 ABY]], the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Zonnos Anjiliac Priare|Zonnos]] secretly installed crab tracers aboard the [[Suwantek Systems|Suwantek]] [[TL-1200 transport]] ''[[New Ambition]]'' to allow [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]] of the [[Bomu Clan]] to locate and attack the [[Starship/Legends|vessel]].
 
==Description==
Crab tracers were minute, autonomous electronic [[Homing beacon/Legends|tracking devices]]. Though not sufficiently intelligent to be classified as [[Droid/Legends|droids]], crab tracers had complex programming. They were designed to slip onto targets silently and undetected. The tracers had six [[Limb/Legends|legs]] that they used to move about and a saucer that could extend or withdraw. They weighed 0.1 [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]] and typically cost {{Cr}}3,000.<ref name="Tempest Feud" />
 
Once in place, the tracers could communicate their locations via the [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]] by use of a miniturized [[Subspace transceiver/Legends|hypertranceiver]]. They transmitted the location of a target even while traveling in [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] and [[Starship/Legends|vessels]] pursuing a starship where crab tracers had been deployed could lock onto a tracer's signal to assist in targeting the infiltrated starship's weapons systems. Crab tracers could be remotely controlled and directed to return to their remote control device for reassignment to a new target. They could also be shut off manually.<ref name="Tempest Feud" />
 
==History==
[[File:ZTH.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Zonnos, the Hutt who had crab tracers placed aboard ''New Ambition'']]
In [[19 ABY/Legends|19 ABY]], the [[Jedi archivist/Legends|Jedi archivist]] [[Mander Zuma]] and the [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] [[Reen Irana]] and [[Eddey Be'ray]]<ref name="Scourge">[[Scourge (novel)|''Scourge'']]</ref> were assigned by [[Popara Anjiliac Diresto|Popara]], the leader of the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Kajidic/Legends|clan]] [[Anjiliac]] to search for Popara's missing son [[Mika Anjiliac Chiera|Mika]] on the [[Quarantine of Endregaad|quarantined]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Endregaad]].<ref name="Tempest Feud" /> While docked on the world [[Makem Te/Legends|Makem Te]], the trio took aboard their vessel, the [[Suwantek Systems|Suwantek]] [[TL-1200 transport]]<ref name="Tempest Feud" /> ''[[New Ambition]]'',<ref name="Scourge" /> supplies of [[medicinal spice]] for distribution to [[Endregaad Plague|plague]] victims on Endregaad. Eager to prevent Mika's rescue, Popara's elder son [[Zonnos Anjiliac Priare|Zonnos]] secretly had crab tracers installed inside the frames of four packets of the medicinal spice cargo aboard<ref name="Tempest Feud" /> ''New Ambition''.<ref name="Scourge" />
 
While<ref name="Tempest Feud" /> ''New Ambition''<ref name="Scourge" /> was en-route to Endregaad, the crab tracers activated, allowing the [[Bomu Clan]], a family of [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]] contracted by Zonnos, to track the Suwantek [[Transport/Legends|transport]]. As<ref name="Tempest Feud" /> ''New Ambition''<ref name="Scourge" /> approached Endregaad, it was ambushed by the Bomu Clan [[YV-260 light freighter]] [[Vengeance (YV-260 light freighter)|''Vengeance'']], which locked onto the signal transmitted by the crab tracers to target the Suwantek vessel.<ref name="Tempest Feud" /> However, the Bomu vessel was destroyed by [[Corporate Sector Authority/Legends|Corporate Sector Authority]] forces that had placed Endregaad under quarantine.<ref name="Scourge" />
 
==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|So nice to see you. Time for you to die.|A member of the Bomu Clan in ''Tempest Feud'', if the Bomu Clan locate the players on the surface of Endregaad using crab tracers|<ref name="Tempest Feud" />}}
Crab tracers appeared in the [[2002]] [[Wizards of the Coast]] [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] adventure ''[[Tempest Feud]]'', by [[Jeff Grubb]] and [[Owen K.C. Stephens]]. The roleplaying adventure was designed to be set in any era from the reign of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] to the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]],<ref name="Tempest Feud" /> however the [[2012]] novel [[Scourge (novel)|''Scourge'']], an adaptation of ''Tempest Feud'', later dated the events of the roleplaying adventure to 19 ABY.<ref name="Scourge" />
 
In the ''Tempest Feud'', the players roleplay as individuals hired by Popara to rescue Mika on Endregaad and it is possible en-route to Endregaad for the players to find and destroy the crab tracers that are aboard<ref name="Tempest Feud" /> ''New Ambition''.<ref name="Scourge" /> If the crab tracers are not destroyed, after the players arrive on Endregaad, the Bomu Clan track down the Suwantek vessel again using the tracers and ambush the player characters on the planet surface.<ref name="Tempest Feud" /> No such ambush is depicted in ''Scourge''<ref name="Scourge" /> hence this outcome is assumed to not form part of the official course of events in [[Star Wars Legends|Star Wars ''Legends'']] continuity.
 
At the conclusion of ''Tempest Feud'', as part of a reward for thwarting the distribution of the spice tempest by Mika, Popara's former intermediary [[Vago Gejalli Thokka|Vago]] offers the player characters a set of four crab tracers for their personal use.<ref name="Tempest Feud" /> In ''Scourge'', Zuma, Irana and Be'ray take the place of the player characters in ''Tempest Feud''<ref name="Tempest Feud" /><ref name="Scourge" /> and no such gift is depicted in their meeting with Vago following Mika's defeat.<ref name="Scourge" /> It is therefore assumed that the gifting of the crab tracers by Vago is not part of official continuity.
